question.problem: A new drug has a $64%$ probability of curing a patient within a week. If $50$ patients are treated, what is the standard deviation of the number of cured patients within a week? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be the number of cured patients within a week.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=50$ patients in the sample

- the probability that the new drug has cured a patient within a week is $p=64%=0.64$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(50,0.64).$ 

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the number of cured patients within a week is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{(50)(0.64)(1-0.64)} \\  & =\sqrt{(50)(0.64)(0.36)} \\  & =\sqrt{11.52} \\  & ≈3.394\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
